Hi there. I'm just going to throw this out here and see what comes of it. I might post this call to action a couple of times depending on the response.

Some back story: I had an idea many years ago, before YouTube was even a thing, to offer a place where people could load their pictures and videos and share them with the world. I know, sounds so cliche today, but this was back in the day. Anyway, I sought out to find the perfect URL to go with the idea: I wanted people to be able to exchange their pictures and videos with ease over the internet, so I combined the first two letters of each of my wants PIcture VIdeo eXchange and came up with PIVIX. So I purchased pivix.com with great intent and high hopes.

Many years later...like over 10.

I've still not pulled off my original intended use for the URL. There have been iterations and re-purposing of the URL, but nothing like what I envisioned for it. I thought it was all a done deal after Imgur lit up the net and earned so much Reddit trust and VC seed money. That was until voat.co users starting requesting for an alternative.

Let's face it, it is going to take skill, time and interested motivated people to pull it off. I'm not looking to be some sort of overlord with a "Mine! Mine! IT'S ALL MINE!" attitude. I think if we can come together and make this thing a reality in the shortest period of time; there is no reason we can't decentralize it and start to pay content creators for the use of their uploaded content to share. All in bitcoin perhaps.

What do you say? I've got the domain, which by the way I have had for over a decade and was recently approached to sell for over $20,000.00 and I refused - they didn't want a site, they wanted the domain. I know, right.

But I'm more than willing to use it and split it up into a community owned operation that best benefits us all if others with skill, time, interested motivation come forward and help bring it into reality.

For the voat.co community.

Let me know your thoughts.

Respectfully,

Jivicus

Why are earthquakes always revised down in scale?

The scale they use, the Richter scale, basically is a way to tell how strong an earthquake is. The weaker the earthquake, the lower the number. So an earthquake with a rating of 1.0 is weaker than an earthquake of 2.0. However, it isn't 1/2 the strength, because the Richter scale goes up by a magnitude of 10 each time, meaning a 2.0 is 10 times stronger than a 1.0, and a 3.0 is 10 times stronger than a 2.0. The scale doesn't perfectly show how much damage it did though, it's more of a tool for geologists to study the way that earthquakes happen and when they happen. The damage from a really big earthquake, take the 2001 Nisqually Earthquake for example (a 6.8 on the Richter scale) was less damaging than other, weaker earthquakes, such as the 1965 Olympia earthquake (a 6.5) that caused 3 deaths compared to the 2001 earthquake's 1 death, because of where they were located. If the 2001 earthquake had been in a more densely populated area then there would have been much more damage, like there was in 1965.
